internal.title: Incident Summary: Accounting Service Kafka Consumer Lag and Latency Issues
internal.body:
At 10:24 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for high Kafka consumer lag in the accounting service, indicating a backlog of 5200 records and elevated p95 latency of 5200 ms. Initial diagnosis confirmed latency issues causing the backlog. Several remediation proposals involving enabling failure flags were blocked by guardrails due to policy constraints. The incident was escalated for further investigation and resolution.

Impact: The accounting service experienced delayed processing due to Kafka consumer lag and increased latency, potentially affecting downstream financial operations.

Root Cause: High Kafka consumer lag and latency in the accounting service caused processing delays. No direct error injection or resource exhaustion was confirmed as the root cause.

Resolution: The incident was escalated for deeper investigation and mitigation. Guardrails prevented some automated remediation actions, requiring manual intervention.

Lessons Learned:
- Guardrails can prevent automated remediation actions; ensure fallback manual procedures are ready.
- Monitoring Kafka consumer lag and latency metrics is critical for early detection of processing delays.
- Error rate alone may not indicate root cause; corroborate with latency and resource metrics.

Action Items:
- Review and update guardrail policies to balance safety and remediation agility.
- Enhance alerting to include combined latency and lag thresholds.
- Conduct training on manual intervention procedures when automated actions are blocked.
